headline: Northcape Capital views Qantas Project Sunrise as value accretive following Airbus Toulouse site visit, reaffirming bullish stance on QAN.
reasoning: Craig McCourtie attended the unveiling of the Airbus A350-1000 ULR at Toulouse in June 2026 and came away with increased conviction that Project Sunrise is value accretive. Operating risk is assessed as lower than expected given the A350 platform's decade-plus service history and proven Rolls-Royce engines, with the primary innovations being incremental rather than radical. Competitive dynamics are highly favourable: no other airline is expected to receive a comparable aircraft before at least 2032, giving Qantas a multi-year window of advantage on ultra long-haul non-stop routes. Returns on capital are expected to exceed the cost of capital, and the new aircraft also unlocks additional upside through more efficient deployment of the existing fleet across the broader network.

Revenue per seat kilometre is expected to increase by approximately 30%, driven by a combination of higher pricing and a greater mix of premium seating, while costs appear stable. Demand for premium, non-stop travel is already well established. In summary, the project appears value accretive, with returns on capital expected to exceed the cost of capital while further strengthening Qantas' competitive position in international markets. The introduction of ultra long-haul aircraft also presents additional upside through more efficient deployment of the existing fleet across the broader network.

With strong free cash flow yields, selective value is emerging in the sector. Northcape retains a modest ~3% exposure.
quote: In insurance, much of the de-rating reflects concern around AI-driven commoditisation, though many risks remain conceptual and are mitigated by industry moats such as scale, product differentiation and supply chain dependencies. With strong free cash flow yields, selective value is emerging, and we retain a modest exposure (~3%).

headline: Praemium cutting ~30% of workforce in response to AI, flagged alongside WiseTech as a potentially defensive cost-cutting reaction
reasoning: Northcape cites Praemium as among the companies cutting aggressively (~30% of workforce) in response to AI. Per Northcape's framework, this is characterised as a defensive reaction typical of weaker business models, rather than the reinvestment approach taken by stronger franchises like HUB24 and Netwealth.
quote: Some companies have moved aggressively to cut costs (e.g. Block cutting ~50% of their workforce this year; WiseTech and Praemium ~30%), while others continue to reinvest (e.g. HUB24, Netwealth, CBA). While markets have rewarded short-term margin improvement, we believe stronger franchises are using AI to extend their advantage, whereas weaker models are reacting defensively.

headline: Erdoğan's escalating judicial crackdown on opposition ahead of 2028 elections raises political risk for Turkish investors
reasoning: Erdoğan has used control of the courts with ruthless efficiency against Istanbul Mayor İmamoğlu, the most likely challenger in the 2028 presidential election. Legal challenges include revocation of İmamoğlu's university diploma (disqualifying him from running), new political espionage charges, and a 4,000-page indictment carrying a potential combined sentence of up to 2,430 years. The appointment of Istanbul's Chief Public Prosecutor — the architect of the opposition crackdown — as Justice Minister in February 2026 signals that legal pressure on the opposition will intensify heading into 2028. Northcape's discussions in Turkey found wide agreement that the political situation has deteriorated over the past two years, associated with high-level corruption impairing economic growth.
quote: On 10 February 2026, Erdoğan appointed Akın Gürlek – previously Istanbul's Chief Public Prosecutor – as Türkiye's new Justice Minister. By elevating the prosecutor who led the legal campaign against his main political rival to the position of Justice Minister, Erdoğan has effectively placed the architect of the opposition crackdown in charge of Türkiye's entire judicial system. Thus, legal pressure on the opposition is likely to intensify heading into the 2028 election. Amongst the discussions we had in Türkiye there was wide agreement that the political situation within the sovereign has deteriorated over the past two years, including continued harassment of journalists. This has been associated with high-level corruption, impairing economic growth.

headline: Northcape Capital designates Turkey as a 'Least Preferred' sovereign and will not invest client capital there despite headline macro improvements
reasoning: Northcape visited Turkey in 2026 and concluded the situation has deteriorated further over the past two years, despite surface-level improvements in economic policy under Finance Minister Şimşek. The firm applies a Cost of Equity hurdle rate of 38% for Turkish companies, which it says completely disqualifies the capital market. Political risk is the core concern: all power is increasingly concentrated in President Erdoğan's hands, creating volatility and the risk of sudden shocks such as sacking Şimşek. The firm draws an explicit parallel to Putin's Russia, noting that foreign investors suffered 100% capital losses when Russia invaded Ukraine. Additional systemic risks include Turkey's high reliance on imported oil, trade links to Iran, and the spectre of EU/US sanctions if a popular uprising leads to violent crackdowns.
quote: We therefore continue to see Türkiye as one of our 'Least Preferred' sovereigns post our visit in 2026, despite the headline improvements in economic policy. We currently use a very high Cost of Equity at 38% as our hurdle rate in valuing Turkish companies, which completely disqualifies this capital market. As such, we will continue to avoid placing any of our client's capital in front of the Türkiye investment proposition.

headline: AI is driving meaningful de-rating across Australian technology and insurance sectors as investors reassess competitive moats, duration risk and terminal value assumptions
reasoning: The February reporting season confirmed AI is now influencing valuation outcomes, not just thematic discussion. Across Australian technology and insurance, there has been meaningful de-rating in businesses perceived to face AI disruption risk even where operating performance was sound. AI reduces the cost and time to build software and launch new business models, eroding the scarcity value that historically supported SaaS pricing power. Northcape believes the impact will not be uniform: businesses with network effects, proprietary data, physical-world integration, or those in high-trust or compliance-heavy environments should prove more resilient, while companies reliant on historical development effort as a moat, extracting economic rents, or combining low profitability with high valuations face greater structural risk.
quote: Across the Australian market, particularly in technology and insurance, we have seen meaningful de-rating in businesses perceived to face AI disruption risk. In many cases, operating performance was sound, yet share prices weakened as investors reassessed duration, competitive intensity and terminal value assumptions under greater uncertainty. The de-rating in technology reflects lower perceived barriers to entry. AI is reducing the cost and time required to build software and launch new business models, eroding the scarcity value that historically supported SaaS pricing power. Investors are therefore less willing to capitalise long-duration earnings at elevated multiples.

headline: Political concentration of power under Erdoğan is the primary risk factor for Turkish capital markets, with the sacking of Finance Minister Şimşek seen as a key tail-risk event
reasoning: Northcape highlights that all power in Turkey is increasingly concentrated in President Erdoğan's hands, making the situation highly volatile and subject to unexpected shocks. The firm draws an explicit parallel to Putin's Russia, warning that Erdoğan could undertake misguided actions that severely undermine credibility, capital markets, and the currency. Sacking Finance Minister Şimşek is identified as the most obvious potential trigger for rapid confidence loss. With presidential elections approaching in 2028 and some alternative leadership approaches in 2024, the probability of destabilising events is seen as rising. A popular uprising — as seen in Syria, Egypt and Iran — is also flagged as an extremely disruptive tail risk that could bring EU and US sanctions into play.
quote: In many ways the Turkish authoritarian government looks a lot like Putin's regime in Russia. We saw what happened to foreign investors in Russia when it invaded Ukraine (100% capital loss). Whilst we do not see Türkiye undertaking a foreign military adventure, Erdoğan could undertake other misguided actions that severely undermine its credibility, capital markets, and currency. Sacking the finance minister, Şimşek, is an obvious potential event in Türkiye that would see confidence rapidly drain from the market.

headline: Turkish inflation remains sticky at ~30% in early 2026 despite tight monetary policy, with consensus forecasts of 26-30% for full year 2026
reasoning: Despite the Turkish Central Bank maintaining the policy rate above 45% from late 2023 to early 2025, inflation has only reduced slowly and is running at approximately 30% in early 2026. A key driver of sticky inflation is continued significant minimum wage increases — set at 27% for 2026, roughly in line with expected inflation. The fiscal deficit has also expanded since 2023 though reconstruction spending from the 2023 earthquakes is expected to wind down, with the central government budget deficit expected to narrow to 3.6% of GDP in 2026 from 4.3% in 2025. The hyperinflation of 70%+ seen in 2021-2022 has passed, but the environment remains challenging for a rapid disinflation.
quote: Despite the Turkish Central Bank setting the policy rate (1-Week Repo rate) above 45% from late 2023 to early 2025, inflation has proven 'sticky' and only reduced slowly over 2024 and 2025 such that it is running at approximately 30% in early 2026. This has meant that the Central Bank has only reduced rates slowly to ensure continued real interest rates and tight monetary policy. One key reason for this sticky inflation is continued significant increases in the minimum wage rate in Türkiye. In 2026 the minimum wage increase has been set at 27%, this compares to inflation which is expected to increase by 26% to 30%.

headline: Anti-American sentiment from the Gaza conflict has hit Coca-Cola sales more severely in Turkey than in other EM markets including Pakistan and Iraq
reasoning: A discussion with the main Coca-Cola bottler in Turkey revealed that anti-American sentiment stemming from the conflict in Gaza has had a more significant negative impact on Coke's sales in Turkey than in other regional markets including Pakistan and Iraq. This was cited in the context of Turkey's growing Islamisation trend and creeping conservatism, which is also shaping consumer behaviour. The observation highlights idiosyncratic demand risks for consumer brands with Western associations operating in Turkey.
quote: Our discussion with the main Coca-Cola bottler in Türkiye highlighted this trend: anti-American sentiment from the conflict in Gaza has impacted Coke's sales much more significantly in Türkiye than other markets including Pakistan and Iraq.

headline: Northcape holds Catapult Sports as a resilient software position with physical-world integration insulating it from AI disruption risk
reasoning: Catapult Sports is named as part of Northcape's ~5% software exposure, concentrated in resilient businesses. Catapult's physical-world integration in sports performance analytics aligns with Northcape's AI resilience framework, which identifies physical-world integration as a key protective moat against AI disruption and commoditisation of software.
quote: Our portfolio remains largely insulated from direct AI disruption. Most holdings derive earnings from physical or financial assets, with limited software exposure (~5%), concentrated in resilient businesses such as REA Group, HUB24 and Catapult Sports.

headline: ASX300 rose 3.9% in February to record highs but returns were heavily concentrated in the five largest stocks, with the median stock falling 1.5%
reasoning: The February 2026 Australian reporting season saw the ASX300 reach new record highs, but returns were extraordinarily concentrated. The five largest companies (major banks and BHP) rose an average of 14%, while the rest of the index was roughly flat and the median stock fell 1.5%, underperforming the index by 5.4%. Sector performance diverged sharply, with Financials (+9.1%), Materials (+8.9%) and Consumer Staples (+5.3%) leading, while Healthcare (-13%) and Technology (-8.1%) significantly underperformed. Northcape's portfolio companies reported aggregate revenue growth of 7% and EPS growth of 10% year-on-year, or 6% and 7% respectively excluding resources.
quote: The Australian market (ASX300) rose 3.9% during the month to reach new record highs, but the strength of the headline index masked an extraordinary concentration of returns. The five largest companies in the ASX (the major banks and BHP) rose by an average of 14% during the month, while the remainder of the ASX300 was roughly flat. In fact, the median stock in the ASX300 fell by 1.5%, underperforming the index by 5.4%.
